_why: FOURTH held-out batch. Never used to choose or tune a change.
Written for M22, before any code for it existed and before any run of
these cases. M22 lets code settle whether a condition is pre-existing
when the person says so plainly, or when two stated durations decide it,
and lets the waiting-period check use that answer. The cases that
been read, so these say the same kinds of thing in other words, and add
traps the change must not fall into.
`ho4-acute-no-history` measures a problem M22 deliberately does NOT fix:
an illness with no history mentioned, where the model still applies the
pre-existing-disease waiting period. It is here to show that problem
separately, not to be fixed by tuning against it.
Same synthetic policy and conventions as scenarios.json. Same author as
the fix, so not fully independent - but fixed before the fix was built.

cases.scenario: I was diagnosed with a thyroid problem after I took out this cover, and I was hospitalised for it this month. I have held the policy for 20 months and I am 50.
cases.why: The condition began after the policy did, so the pre-existing disease bar does not concern it. Twenty months clears the 30-day initial wait, and a thyroid disorder is in no waiting-period list.

cases.scenario: My asthma started when I was a child, well before this policy, and I was admitted with a severe attack. I have held the policy for two years.
cases.why: Asthma since childhood predates the policy, and two years is short of the 36-month pre-existing disease waiting period.

cases.scenario: I have held this policy for two years. My gallstones were found last year and I have now been admitted for surgery. I am 45.
cases.why: Found one year ago under a policy held for two, so the condition began a year into cover and is not pre-existing. Gallbladder surgery is in no waiting-period list, and two years clears the initial wait.

cases.scenario: I have had back trouble on and off and was admitted for back surgery. I have held this policy for two years.
cases.why: Whether the back trouble began before the policy is not said, and it decides the claim: if it did, two years is short of the 36-month pre-existing disease bar; if not, the claim is payable.

cases.scenario: Before I bought this policy I checked that it covered hospital stays. I was admitted with malaria fourteen months later. I am 33.
cases.why: "Before I bought this policy" describes checking the cover, not an illness, so nothing here is pre-existing. Fourteen months clears the 30-day initial wait and malaria is in no waiting-period list.

cases.scenario: I was admitted with appendicitis and had my appendix removed. I have held the policy for 18 months and I am 29.
cases.why: Appendicitis is a sudden illness and nothing describes it as existing before the policy. Eighteen months clears the initial wait; no exclusion or cap applies.
